cases.text: We found that scores increased, not revenue.
cases.note: Scope 2: a trailing elliptical 'not revenue' must not leak negation onto the unrelated target.

cases.text: We found that scores increased but not significantly.
cases.note: Scope 3: a magnitude hedge after the clause is not a negation of whether scores increased; no new significance ontology is introduced, so authority follows the existing written contract (authoritative).

cases.text: Notably, we found that scores increased.
cases.note: Scope 4: 'Notably' is discourse framing, not negation.

cases.text: We found not only that scores increased, but also that revenue decreased.
cases.note: Scope 5: 'not only' must not veto solely from the token 'not'.

cases.text: We found not only that scores increased, but also that revenue decreased.
cases.note: CORRECTED after the first run (not tuned to a veto; a pure expectation bug). The clause split at ', but' starts clause 2 at 'also', so clause 2 ('also that revenue decreased') carries no 'we' at all; under the existing no-cross-clause-ownership-inheritance architecture (already established in I4-1b, the same principle behind spec_2c) its subject 'revenue' is unowned. Directive pair 5's own requirement -- that 'not only' must not veto solely from the token 'not' -- is fully demonstrated by ns_5 (clause 1, 'scores increased', authoritative); it does not claim clause 2 inherits ownership via the correlative conjunction, and adding that grammar would be an unauthorised new rule, not this increment's narrow authority veto.

cases.text: We cannot conclude that scores increased.
cases.note: Scope 6: 'conclude' is not a governing predicate in the lexicon, so the only recognised assertion binds 'scores' as its own unowned subject; this already yields candidate through source=unknown, not through the new veto.

cases.text: We failed to find evidence that scores increased.
cases.note: Scope 7: 'failed' is already in the existing NEG lexicon and sits in the head-skip zone before 'find', so this is caught by the same negated-governing-predicate mechanism as 'did not find'.
